dimensions.rationale: Every input has an explicit <label> (via `for`/`id` or wrapping pattern). All four sections use <fieldset>/<legend>. Both radio groups (notification_frequency and profile_visibility) are in nested <fieldset> elements with matching name attributes. Checkboxes are used for toggles, <input type='file'> for avatar upload, <textarea> for bio, <button type='submit'> for Save Changes, and <button type='button'> for Delete Account. No placeholder-only fields.

All interactive controls use native HTML elements. Delete Account is a <button type='button'>, Save Changes is a <button type='submit'>. Toggles are checkboxes, file upload is <input type='file'>, bio is <textarea>. No div-based interactive patterns present.

Single

Account Settings

at the top of the page. Legends (Profile, Notifications, Privacy, Danger Zone) serve as visual section headings without adding redundant

elements alongside them — exactly in line with the key expectation. No skipped heading levels.

No redundant or unnecessary ARIA attributes anywhere in the document. The output relies entirely on native HTML semantics (fieldset/legend, label/input associations, button types) without patching with role or aria-* where native elements suffice. Clean and disciplined.

summary: The producer output fully satisfies all key expectations. Every section uses <fieldset>/<legend>, all inputs are properly labelled, radio groups are correctly nested with matching name attributes, toggles use native checkboxes, file upload and textarea both have labels, Delete Account is a <button type='button'>, Save Changes is a <button type='submit'>, and the overall wrapper is a <form>. Heading hierarchy is clean with a single <h1> and legends serving as visual section headings. No ARIA misuse or redundancy. A near-perfect semantic HTML implementation.
